events-bus-emit: The TS funnel emits every gameStatusUpdate twice: as a frontend message and on the backend event bus (sendGameStatusUpdate). Nothing outside tests listens: a grep of src and meta for on('gameStatusUpdate'/once(/addListener( at HEAD (88.3-01) finds one match, the engineWineResolvers test, and the only bus listeners in non-test code are 'releasesInfoReady', 'settingChanged' and the per-app 'progressUpdate-<app>' of installStallWatchdog. So the Rust funnel emits only the frontend message; the bus entries of the golden are recorded for completeness and the replay skips them.
reads-folded-into-launch-facts: The TS recorder lists the play marker and every read the TS funnel made: game.getSettings, config.getSettings (three to five times per launch) and gameConfigs.get(app).getSettings (the verboseLogs read, a different store from the game settings). The Rust funnel asks the managers once, with launch_facts, before it does anything, so none of those reads is an event of the Rust funnel and the replay drops those kinds from the golden. What the reads returned is still compared: it is the input of every later event.
rejection-text-is-a-fixed-word: The TS funnel rejected a Play with the rejecting collaborator's own message (a failed engine step, a rejected before or after script, a rejected GOG playtime post). Rust never carries that text: a step, script or hook failure is a fixed category word (T-88.2-14, T-88.3-09), so a rejected Play answers launch:<what>:<word> and the replay compares the golden's rejection with a Rust one, not the message. What was done before the rejection, and what was left undone after it, is compared event for event.
recent-game-warning-text: The TS warning for a rejected recent-game write passed two arguments (the text and the error) and the recorder kept both as a list; the Rust line is one string with the fixed reason of the op (no Error class prefix). The replay joins the golden's parts with a space and drops the Error prefix before comparing.
warning-prefix-is-an-options-object: The TS passed the playtime-sync-disabled warning's prefix as an options object ({ prefix: 'Backend' }), which the logger reads as the Backend prefix, and the recorder kept the argument as given. Rust writes the prefix itself, so the replay reads the golden's object as the prefix it names.
hook-error-lines-are-the-managers: The TS funnel wrote the error lines around a rejected syncSaves (Error while downloading saves for <title>. <error>, Error uploading saves ...) and a rejected game.launch (the exception into gamelib.log and the game's log) itself, with the error text. In Rust a hook whose TS call throws answers a fixed category and the TS handler behind the hook (88.3-08) writes its own error line, so no error text crosses into Rust (T-88.2-14); the replay's recording hooks write those lines to the tape at the same place, and the funnel's own events around them are compared.
release-warning-is-a-fixed-word: The TS warning for an engine release that failed (the app is quitting, or the channel rejected) printed String(error) after 'could not release its launch:'. Rust never carries a collaborator's error text into gamelib.log (T-88.3-09), so the line carries the fixed word of the step (rejected); the replay reads the golden's text up to the colon and compares the rest as that word. Which launch ended without replacing its result or error is compared event for event.
